answer: Sequential delay proofs resist sybils: each new identity must complete a verifiable delay function that takes real wall-clock time and cannot be sped up by running many copies in parallel, like an ember that must burn down before the next branch is planted in the orchard. An attacker wanting ten thousand fake agents must wait ten thousand sequential delays, while one honest agent waits once, and each finished proof anchors a single vertex in the identity graph. The limit is latency: honest onboarding also slows, so delays must stay short and pair with rate caps, not serve as the only gate.
